title.narrative: Stöd UN Womens interim landprogram DRK
Support to UN Women interim strategic note DRC

description.narrative:
Ambassaden kommer att stödja UN Womens landkontor under den sista fasen av sin strategiska plan 2014-2017, som har förlängts till 2019, samt lanseringen av sin nya strategiska plan från 2020. Stödet är en övergångsfinansiering på 9 månader. Intentionen är att ambassaden ska ge långsiktigt stöd för den nya strategiska planen från 2020, och möjligheten att göra så kommer att bedömmas under slutet av 2019.
Målet med den strategiska planen för 2014-2017 som förlängdes fram till 2019, är att stödja den kongolesiska regeringen och det civila samhället och andra berörda aktörer att genomföra, övervaka och rapportera om DRKs åtaganden om jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt. UN Womens grundläggande roll i DRK är att tillhandahålla stöd till nyckelpartner och aktörer, ge tekniskt stöd och expertis, främja effektiv samordning / uppföljning / utvärdering, dokumentera resultat, samt att generera och främja användningen av sex-disaggregerad data. De fokusområden som beskrivs i den strategiska noten är följande: samordning; stärkt jämställdhetsperspektiv av planering och budgetering; våld mot kvinnor och flickor; kvinnor, fred och säkerhet; kvinnors politiska ledarskap och deltagande; samt kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt. Av dessa har tre områden prioriterats mer specifikt av UN Women när förlängningen av den strategiska planen godkändes 2017: kvinnor, fred och säkerhet; inklusive könsbaserat våld; kvinnors politiska ledarskap och deltagande; och kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt. Dessa alla motsvarar ambassadens och Sida prioriteringar.

The embassy will support the UN Women DRC office in the final period of implementation of their strategic note 2014-2017, extended until 2019, and the launch of their new strategic note from 2020. The support is a bridge funding to cover 9 months. The intention is for the embassy to continue to support the new strategic note from 2020, and the feasibility of doing so will be assessed during the latter part of 2019.
The goal of the strategic note for the 2014 - 2017, extended until 2019, is to support the Congolese government and civil society, and other concerned actors to implement, monitor and report on DRC's commitments to gender equality and women's empowerment. The fundamental role of UN Women in DRC is to accompany key partners and actors, provide technical support and expertise, promote effective coordination/monitoring/evaluation, document results, generate and promote the use of sex disaggregated data. The focus areas as outlined in the strategic note are as follows: coordination; gender responsive planning and budgeting; violence against women and girls; women, peace and security; women's political leadership and participation; women's economic empowerment. Three areas were prioritized further by UN Women when the extension of the strategic note was agreed in 2017: Women, peace and security, including SGBV; women's political leadership and participation; and women's economic empowerment. These all correspond to priorities of the embassy and Sida.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
As specified in the objective of the intervention, the purpose with this contribution was to support the implementation of the UN Women DRC Strategic note and annual work plan 2014-2017, extended until 2019, and the development of the new strategic note 2020-2024. In other words, Sweden entered as a donor for the Strategic Note during its extended period as a bridging support through the development of the new Strategic Note leading to its adoption and for that, a specific contribution.
During the activity period of this contribution, the new strategic Note was developed, adopted and made the main objective of a new Sida contribution with support to UN Women, 12402.
This project, in terms of the implementation of the previous strategic note extended for the period of this project, was implemented in a rapidly changing environment on different levels, most notably the aftermath of the December 2018 elections and the global threat of the Covid-19 pandemic and restrictions following the pandemic causing limitation on activities and effecting women's and girls' lives. Nevertheless, in the framework of the national evaluation conducted on the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action, some key commitments towards a more equal Congolese society have been taken during the last 12 months, such as the adoption of the updated national strategy on sexual and gender based violence (SGBV) and the second generation National Action Plan for the UNSCR 1325. In this, UN Women plaid a large part. UN Women was also, in spite of the difficult and sometime volatile situation in the country, able to carry out multiple activities and projects and reach results in each of the four pillars (1. Women's political participation and engagement in decision-making (WPP); 2. Women's economic empowerment (WEE); 3. Women, peace, security and humanitarian action (WPS/HA); and 4. Gender coordination). The following are examples of these achievements and results.
To effectively play a leading role in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment UN Women formed strategic partnership with state actors, civil society organisations and UN agencies. Key partners from these different categories were involved in the implementation of the strategic note, notably through partnership agreements.
Training on gender and local governance was performed in Kinshasa for provincial deputies. Following the training, a network of elected women at the provincial and local level was set up allowing for exchange of information, sharing of experiences and implementation of strategies to advance the gender agenda within the provincial assemblies as well as allowing elected women to develop collective leadership within the framework of their parliamentary mandate.
In a context of decentralisation, UN Women together with joint UNDP and the Ministry of decentralisation performed trainings in which UN Women had a module on gender institutionalisation. During the training, UN Women distributed a manual developed for integrating gender into parliamentary practices to provide parliamentarians and provincial ministers in several provinces with tools for integrating gender into development policies and programs at the provincial level.
For the purpose of women's economic empowerment, a network of rural women's associations was set up and launched in Kinshasa with the participation of 12 provinces (Central Kongo, Kinshasa, Kwilu, Kasai Central, Kasai Oriental, North Kivu, South Kivu, Equateur, Tshopo, Maniema, Haut Katanga and Lualaba) and it counted, at its creation, 1,982 associations with more than 50,000 active members.
In Kinshasa, 255 women received training and acquired skills in cassava processing and strengthened their knowledge on agribusiness basic notions thus improving their families food security and income diversity. Another 100 women farmers acquired new knowledge and improved their skills on management, processing and marketing techniques for agricultural products (cassava and soybean).
In response to the Covid-19 crisis, more than 400 women were sensitised to use the ZOOM app for online training and meetings in times of crises, trained in technical skills such as antiseptic soap and hydroalcoholic gel making. Also in relation to the Covid-19 emergency, 800 women and girls received information useful for the prevention of Covid-19 for themselves, their families and their communities as well as resilience kits including masks, bleach bottles, hydroalcoholic gel, soap, sanitary towels and several food items that could help them comply with the containment measures.
Humanitarian teams in Central Kasai, Tanganyika, North and South Kivu have improved their humanitarian interventions by taking into account the gender dimension thanks to 129 (58 women and 71 men) humanitarian actors who have strengthened their capacity to take gender into account in emergencies and who have now made a commitment to take into account the specific needs of men and women, boys and girls and other specific groups including people living with disabilities, people living with HIV, members of the LGBT community, etc.
The Swedish funding allowed the measurement of the socio-economic impacts of conflicts and humanitarian crises on women and girls through a field study conducted in five pilot provinces (North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Tanganyika and Kasai); the results showed that, despite precarious situations, women, girls, men and boys are differently affected during conflicts, health crises and natural disasters. Men and boys are at greater risk of being recruited into armed militias and of being killed or injured; however, the majority of women and girls interviewed have experienced sexual violence, particularly in remote areas during forced displacement. Women's rights are generally undermined: poor access to sexual and reproductive health services, hygiene conditions not adapted to women's specific needs, constant increase of GBV cases, lack of food, decent and secured housing, poor access to education, difficulty in controlling family resources, low representation of women.
In relation to the UNSCR 1325, 177 participants (80 women and 97 men) representing CSOs, gender divisions, security services (PNC, DGM, FARDC), justice, religious and traditional leaders, and the private sector from Bukavu, Goma, Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and Kalemie were trained in women's rights and the women, peace and security agenda through awareness-raising sessions on women's rights, on the commitments on women, peace and security, and on Beijing 25; In short, led to the following results. The operationalisation of networks of women-led associations set up and the strengthening of their institutional governance; the establishment of public-private partnerships for an improved sustainability of the initiatives in the agriculture and entrepreneurship; persistence in the dissemination of national laws and policies on gender equality and women's empowerment; the creation of a critical mass of key humanitarian and development actors involved in gender mainstreaming.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
